car.model: Amg E63 S Sedan Final Edition

build_inputs.model: Amg E63 S Sedan Final Edition
build_inputs.angles:
- This is the last V8 E63. Mercedes built 999 Final Editions worldwide and then the V8 E-Class was over -- the generation that replaced it has no V8 at any price.
- 603 horsepower and 627 lb-ft from a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, 3.4 seconds to sixty-two.
- Nothing was added mechanically. Same engine, same output as any E63 S -- the Final Edition is a paint colour, a badge and a goodbye.
- One colour only: Manufaktur Graphite Grey Magno, with yellow stitching and yellow illuminated door sills. Each car carries a console badge with its own build number.
- Japan got 50 of the 999, split 25 left-hand drive and 25 right. Mercedes never published the US allocation or how many were sedans.
- About 12,800 new before the Final Edition premium. The wagons now trade above the sedans.

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2023 Mercedes-AMG E63 S Sedan Final Edition, finished in Graphite Grey Magno with a black and Titanium Grey interior. This E63's odometer currently displays about 300 miles. The attached Carfax history report shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this E63’s brief past. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this E63 S carried an original MSRP of $170,063. Factory equipment includes the Final Edition package, AMG sport suspension, an electronic limited-slip differential, Exclusive Nappa leather and microfiber upholstery, power-adjustable, heated, and ventilated front seats, a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, an MBUX infotainment system with a 12.3-inch touchscreen display, a Burmester surround sound system, and more as detailed below. The seller reports no modifications. Mercedes-AMG launched the Final Edition of the W213-based E63 and E63 S models for the final year of the model’s production. Limited to 999 examples worldwide, the E63 Final Edition was exclusively offered in Graphite Grey Magno, and featured special touches like yellow illuminated AMG door sills, to celebrate the production end of what appears to be the last V8-engined E63 ever. Released for 2018, the W213-based E63 and E63 S arrived with a more fluid design, a smaller yet more powerful engine, and a drift mode that can send 100% of the engine's torque to the rear wheels. Power comes from an M177 twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8, rated at 603 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to all four wheels via a 9-speed multi-clutch automatic transmission and Mercedes-Benz's 4Matic+ configurable all-wheel-drive system.
